_note: Scripted paths for the sample triggers in config/trigger-samples.json, used only when MODEL_PROVIDER=stub. One script per severity band, plus per-sample overrides for sentences that exercise something their band does not. `bands` is matched on the sample's expected tier; `samples` wins when a key matches the sample id. config/stub-script.json is untouched and is still the default take (the clock-driven medication refill).
_limits: A static script cannot quote words it has not seen, so these do not call record_account: the transcript has to be verbatim (R5) and only a real model has the sentence in front of it. They also avoid naming a provider, because provider names live in onboarding data that is all placeholder today. What these scripts do demonstrate is the routing the severity decides: critical acts and settles up afterwards, urgent and routine stop and ask the RP first. A static script also cannot branch on an answer: test_due_tap always closes on the second clinic, whichever of the three buttons is pressed. A real model reads the answer and does what was actually chosen -- including the decline path, where it tells the family and escalates to the RP. The money is the same: spoken_account always scripts the approved path, because a static script cannot know what Arun actually tapped on the receipt. A real model reads his answer and passes through what he really chose -- including the decline, where nothing is debited, no cab is booked and she is not told one is coming. The two taps are the same again at the other end of the call: refill_tap is scripted with the first chemist holding the strip and test_due_tap with the second clinic holding the slot, because a static script cannot branch on what the line actually came back with. A real model hears the out of stock or the fully booked and works down the ranked list instead -- order_medicines and book_test are only reached once somebody has really said yes. test_due_tap and test_due_unavailable are the two ends of the same phone call, split because a static script cannot branch on what the line came back with: the tap books on her own doctor's first free slot, and test_due_unavailable is the same request when he has nothing and the choice goes back to her. A real model hears which one it got and only one of these ever happens. The delivery is scripted on the path where it works: Pillar Road delivers, the counter confirms what it handed over, and Lakshmi confirms she has it. R14 is the other half of that call and a real model has to take it -- a chemist that cannot deliver means arranging a pickup from the nearest chemist and an auto for somebody in the family instead. A static script also cannot wait on the chemist or on Lakshmi, so it stops after asking and picks up again when their confirmation arrives.
_r19: Every turn that calls a tool opens with log_decision. There is no exemption, not even for set_stage.
